## Stages

The order was set by your partner on 2026-11-06: Track A (Stages 1–3) first, then
Track B (Stages 4–6).

This order diverges from the brief's driver order in Part A (seasonality, collection
interval, funding, sample, staffing). It follows information order instead:
- Track A rests on calendar variation from public release dates. That data takes a day
  or two to assemble.
- Stage 1's first fit measures model run time on about 40 years of vintages. That time is
  unknown now, and it sizes every later stage.
- Track B's covariates are slow, collinear and hand-built over several days. Its answer
  does not change Track A's model.

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision scale
      Objective: Estimate how one-month revision size moves with collection days before first release.
      Spec: Brief Part A driver 2; Part B data inventory; Part C (scale estimand, priors, validation, implementation); GPT §2.2, §3.3, §4.4, §4.10–4.14; CL Driver 2, §4.2, §4.8–4.10
      Gap closed: O1; scaffold row
      Consumes: nothing (scaffold only)
      Produces: monthly vintage panel and release calendar, built reproducibly in-repo; baseline revision-scale model; measured wall-clock time of one fit
      Exit: a committed finding under `specs/` reports the O1 estimate with uncertainty, its diagnostics and the measured fit time; the panel build is covered by passing tests
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Late sample vs. seasonal-factor revision
      Objective: Split the one- and two-month revisions into late-sample and seasonal-factor parts.
      Spec: Brief Part A driver 1; Part C (seasonality bullet); GPT §2.1, §4.5; CL Driver 1, §4.5; GM Part A 1
      Gap closed: O3
      Consumes: Stage 1 Produces
      Produces: joint NSA/SA vintage handling; decomposition usable as a control by later stages
      Exit: a committed finding reports the O3 shares by stage, with uncertainty and diagnostics
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: First-closing rate and two-month revision scale
      Objective: Estimate how two-month revision size moves with the first-closing collection rate.
      Spec: Brief Part A driver 2 and revision stage 2; GPT §2.2; CL Driver 2
      Gap closed: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1 and Stage 2 Produces
      Produces: collection-rate series in-repo; Track A scale model with calendar, collection and seasonal terms
      Exit: a committed finding reports the O2 estimate with uncertainty and diagnostics
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Sample size, attrition and revision scale
      Objective: Estimate how revision size moves with CES sample size and attrition.
      Spec: Brief Part A driver 4; Part B data inventory; Part C (identification bullet); GPT §2.4, §4.8; CL Driver 4, §4.7; GM Part A 4, Part C 5

      Exit: a committed finding reports the O6 estimate with uncertainty, or states that it is not identified and why
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and its plan header copies it verbatim:

> Roadmap: specs/ces-revisions-prompt-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

With every stage ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O6 and the scaffold row. Give
evidence per verdict: the implementing stage or plan, any Deviation notes, and any
deferred-item entries.

An unmet row has two exits: a new stage, which keeps the roadmap live, or deferral with a
written reason.

Optional: re-run describe-critique-methodology's Describe mode on the system as built, and
diff the result against the brief.
